title: security: RBAC v2 policy hardening + KMS region-pinning audit logging
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: strengthen RBAC v2 guardrails for KMS-backed key usage and implement region-pinning audit logging required by ENG-3421 and compliance reviews. This PR introduces enforcement toggles, additional audit events for KMS operations, and policy validation to prevent cross-region key usage when a resource is pinned to a data residency region. Changes are scoped to the RBAC v2 subsystem and the audit logger and include a migration path so existing customers on older configs are opt-in for enforcement. Summary of changes: - RBAC v2: added new policy predicates `kmsRegion` and `require_kms_region_match` that allow rules to express region pinning constraints. - Enforcement toggle: new config `rbac.v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning` (default: false) with runtime rollout via rollout flags. - Audit logging: emit `kms.region_mismatch` and `kms.region_pinning_enforced` events with immutable metadata for downstream auditors. - KMS integration: server-side validation during key-attach and key-usage paths to check region residency and deny operations when enforcement is enabled. - Admin tooling: CLI policy linter (rbacctl lint-policy) and migration script to annotate existing policies with explicit kmsRegion fields where possible. - Tests: unit and integration tests exercising policy evaluation, audit event emission, and negative paths. Migration/rollout plan: 1) Deploy with enforcement=false and audits enabled for two weeks. 2) Monitor `kms.region_mismatch` events and surface top offenders via Redwood Console. 3) Enable enforcement for a small set of tenants (canary) and expand after one week of no critical failures. Backwards compatibility: config default disables enforcement to avoid breaking customers; the policy linter can auto-suggest annotations without changing behavior. Checklist: - [x] API and runtime checks implemented - [x] Audit events emitted for all KMS-related decision points - [x] Policy linter and migration script included - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Docs updated (RBAC v2 and compliance guide) - [x] Rollout plan and monitoring dashboard ready Notes: See ENG-3421 and SUP-1287 for compliance context. This PR intentionally avoids automatic rewrites of existing policies; we surface suggestions instead.

release_notes: Harden RBAC v2 with KMS region-pinning predicates and audit logging. Adds a non-breaking enforcement toggle and admin tooling for migration. See docs/security/rbac-v2-kms-region-pinning.md for usage and rollout guidance.
observability_notes: New metrics: rbac.kms.region_mismatch.count and rbac.kms.region_pinning_enforced.count. Dashboard added at redwood/observability/dashboards/kms_region_pinning.json. Audit events: kms.region_mismatch and kms.region_pinning_enforced include policy_id, tenant_id, resource_id, key_id, source_region, key_region, and timestamp.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover predicate logic and nil/edge cases (rbac_kms_predicate_test.go). Integration test exercises key-attach and key-usage flows across region mismatches and validates audit event emission. CI runs full test matrix; flaky tests fixed during PR, final pipeline passed.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy with rbac.v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning=false and enable audit events for 14 days. Stage 2: create canary cohort of 5 tenants, enable enforcement via rollout flags. Stage 3: monitor dashboards and errors for 7 days, expand incrementally. Emergency rollback: flip enforcement flag off and revert rollout flag in service config.
security_impact: Improves security posture by preventing accidental cross-region KMS usage when resources are pinned. Default behavior is opt-in to avoid service disruption. No secret material changes. Security scan passed.
notes_for_ops: When enabling enforcement, expect an increase in `rbac.kms.region_mismatch.count` events for unannotated policies; use the migration script to suggest annotations. Ensure the observability retention for kms_region_pinning dashboard is set to 30d during rollout.
